chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Jaroud Abu Al-Munzir, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The chief of the deeds are three: Fairness with the people from yourself, until you are not pleased with anything except that you are pleased for them with the like of it; and equalizing with the brother in wealth; and remembering Allah upon every state.'
(This remembrance) is not merely saying 'Glory be to Allah, and the Praise is for Allah, and there is no god except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest' alone,
but rather, when something comes to you which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has Commanded, you act upon it; or when something comes to you which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has Forbidden, you leave it.

key_terms.مُوَاسَاتُكَ الْأَخَ فِي الْمَالِ: Equalizing/sharing with the brother in wealth

ai.seo_question: What are the three chief deeds according to Imam al-Sadiq (as)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates self-accountability (muhasabah) and material generosity as foundational to spiritual integrity, framing them alongside a dynamic, action-oriented remembrance of Allah. This triad reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating inner consciousness with outward social justice, where dhikr is validated by adherence to divine command rather than mere ritualistic repetition. The narration underscores that true piety is measured by one's fairness in dealings and willingness to share resources, aligning personal devotion with communal welfare.

en.hubeali: From him, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Jaroud Abu Al Munzir who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The chief of the deeds are three – Fairness with the people from yourself until you are not pleased with something except you are pleased for with the like of it; and your equalising with the brother in the wealth; and remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon every state.

(This is) not (saying), ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and there is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Greatest’, only, but,

when something comes up to you which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Commanded with, you take to it, or when something comes upon you which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Forbidden from, you leave it’.
en.sarwar: It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Aqaba from Jarud from abu al-Mundhir who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘The masters of good deeds are three things: To yield to justice for people against one’s own soul.

So what you do not like to happen to you, do not agree to happen to people also, to cooperate with your fellow believer in matters of properties and to speak of Allah in all conditions: not just saying, ‘Glory belongs to Allah, all praise belongs to Allah and no one deserves to be worshipped except Allah, but that if in case Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has commanded you to do a certain thing, you must obey the command, and if it is a case you know that Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has prohibited you to do, you must stay away form it.’”
